newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call down on lower demand, gilts subdued.
newsitem.headline: Indian call down on lower demand, gilts subdued.

text.p: Indian call money rates eased from opening levels of 6.0-6.75 percent to end Thursday at 4.75-5.25 percent on reduced demand, dealers said.
Call money rates ended Wednesday at 1.5-2.0 percent but opened higher on Thursday morning on fund outflows.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) held a four-day repos auction on Wednesday at which it accepted bids for 41.94 billion rupees, with payments to be made on Thursday.
Dealers said the outflows by successful bidders pushed up call money rates.
"There were a few deals at 6.5 percent in early morning trade," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "But rates fell quickly thereafter as there was not much demand for funds."
"Most banks had already covered their positions ahead of the reporting day tomorrow," he said.
Banks report their positions to the RBI every fortnight and the next reporting day is Friday.
Dealers said the higher call rates led to reduced trading in government securities with prices little changed from Wednesday's levels.
Trades on the National Stock Exchange were worth 1.6 billion rupees against Wednesday's 3.1 billion, dealers said.

The 13.50 percent 1998 government of India stock traded at 103.03 rupees against its last traded price of 103.02, the 13.40 percent 1999 stock eased to 101.75 from 101.76 and the 13.70 percent 1999 stock dropped to 102.73 from 102.78, dealers said.
Treasury bill maturing in March yielded 6.75-6.85 percent, April bills 7.60 percent and May bills 7.70 percent, dealers said.
